entries.name: egrid_boundary_heat_rate_reconciliation
entries.where: src/market_sim/data/fleet/eia860.py::_egrid_boundary_hr_repairs (constants EGRID_CC_HR_PHYSICAL_CEILING / EGRID_COLOCATION_RADIUS_KM / EGRID_UNIT_VINTAGE_TOL_YEARS)
entries.source: eGRID 2023 rev2 UNT23 own-unit heat input (CT-01 + CT-02 = 24,376,259 MMBtu) over PLNT23 PLNGENAN (3,543,044 MWh). Ceiling is HEAT_RATE_BINS['gas_ct']['older'] = 11.5 (EIA Table 8): a combined cycle raises steam from its own topping turbine's exhaust, so it cannot be less efficient than a bare simple-cycle GT of its era.
entries.note: NOT a tunable: zero free parameters, the output value is arithmetic on eGRID's own fields and is never chosen. The three constants are structural thresholds (a physics ceiling, a site-identity radius, a CEMS-vs-EIA commissioning offset), not fitted values; the accepted set is invariant to them over any plausible range except that loosening the ceiling admits known false positives. Re-derive trigger is a new eGRID release (a source-data change), never a residual -- rule 23. A release that fixes the 55641 attribution makes condition 1 stop firing and this a silent no-op.

entries.name: SUMMER_WEFOR_SHARE
entries.where: config/fuel_trajectories.py::SUMMER_WEFOR_SHARE (re-homed by miso-91 from data/fleet/arrays.py::_SUMMER_WEFOR_SHARE; consumed by data.fleet.arrays._apply_thermal_availability)
entries.lineage_solves: NONE - no sweep, derivation or calibration lineage exists for the 0.30
entries.source: UNCITED A-PRIORI HEURISTIC, declared as such. Fraction of a unit's WEFOR applied in the summer peak (Jun-Sep); the remaining (1 - share) is redistributed into the shoulder months, conserving annual outage energy. market-sim-build-plan.md records it as the 'flat per-plant-group POF heuristic' awaiting a data-derived replacement. IMPORTANT ON THE LABEL: it was NEVER FITTED to a residual. It is classified 'residual' because that is the strictest existing enforcement category - audit_keepers.py E8 requires every residual entry to carry an open root cause - NOT because it was tuned. Read it as 'unidentified', which is if anything weaker than residual-fitted: there is no lineage at all. The WEFOR MAGNITUDE it reallocates IS GADS-cited (THERMAL_AVAILABILITY, 'Source: NERC GADS by unit type and age'); only the seasonal reallocation is uncited. MATERIALITY (measured by miso-91, no LP): it governs all SIX non-coal thermal classes under this keeper's flags - COAL is exempt because coal_drop_pof=True routes it to a branch that drops summer WEFOR entirely (measured delta 0.0000). Per-class summer availability the 0.30 adds vs a flat-WEFOR baseline: ST_GAS +14.70 pp, ST_CHP +5.60, CT_PEAKER +4.29, CC_REGULAR +3.15, CT_CHP +3.06, CC_CHP +2.52. Against the committed per-class nameplates (FINDING-miso89 sec.5) that is ~3.9 GW of MISO summer-peak capability at a uniform fleet age of 18 y, ~4.6 GW at 28 y, ~5.8 GW at 38 y. NOTE this corrects the miso-90 finding, which scoped the parameter to CT_PEAKER alone. PHYSICS TENSION: for PLANNED outages, shifting maintenance off the peak is well-founded (and the POF side is separately grounded by the measured MAINTENANCE_MONTHLY_SHAPE); for FORCED outages the reallocation runs OPPOSITE to the physics, since forced outages correlate POSITIVELY with heat and high load. Recorded as an unverified directional argument, not a citation.
entries.root_cause: OPEN ROOT CAUSE - no measured source resolves a seasonal forced-outage shape at the grain this parameter needs. Standing data ask: docs/handoffs/miso-outage-grain-data-ask-2026-07.md (acceptance test part 1 - the source must declare CAPABILITY, not output, which is what rejects CAMPD, EIA-923 and every derivative of either). The class where it binds hardest and is least recoverable is CT_PEAKER: CT down-windows cannot be certified forced-outage vs out-of-merit-at-peak, so every output-derived instrument inherits the defect (adjudicated NO-BUILD on identification grounds, results/calibration/FINDING-miso90-ct-availability-identification-2026-07.md). Until such a source exists the honest disposition is to DECLARE and stop (rule 24), NOT to tune. Re-derivation must cite the data change, never a residual (rule 23 [R-FROZEN-DERIVE]).
entries.forecast_risk: Reproduces in a forecast year by construction (it is a fixed fraction applied to the age-escalated GADS WEFOR), so it is forward-runnable - but it does NOT respond to changed conditions: it carries no weather, load or temperature driver, so a hotter forecast year gets the same 70% summer-outage relief as a mild one. That is the forecast-side cost of the missing measured shape.
entries.prohibition: DO NOT re-tune against a residual (rule 24). Its ~3.9-5.8 GW blast radius is the same order as the ~10 GW summer-peak fossil under-derate ledgered as the C3b caveat, so a hand-set value here would be an answer key for an already-ledgered miss. The C3b ledger explicitly does not license a fitted availability number.

entries.lineage_solves: NONE - no derivation lineage for the 0.10 / 0.125 magnitudes
entries.source: UNCITED FLAT APPROXIMATION of a real, well-established physical effect: gas-turbine output falls as inlet air temperature rises, and simple-cycle CTs lose more than combined-cycle (whose steam bottoming cycle partially compensates). The EFFECT is sound and the sign/ordering are right; the SPECIFIC magnitudes are not traced to a primary source - they are consistent with, but not derived from, the 10-30% typical CT summer derate the repo's own capacity audit records against EIA-860 net-summer ratings (docs/capacity-audit-860-923-campd.md). Two distinct scalars (0.10 CC, 0.125 CT) over four class keys. Labelled 'residual' for the same enforcement reason as SUMMER_WEFOR_SHARE: it was never fitted, but it is unidentified and must carry an open root cause.
entries.root_cause: OPEN but LOWER PRIORITY than SUMMER_WEFOR_SHARE, because the measured alternatives have already been built and adjudicated rather than skipped - so rule 11 [R-ACCURATE] is not engaged. scenario.temp_dependent_derate is a measured per-class dry-bulb curve and is default-off, probe-refuted for the ERCOT gas fleet 2026-07-09. Its MISO sibling scenario.gt_ambient_derate is measured PROVABLY INERT: MISO zone-mean TMAX clears its 35 C reference in 0 h at summer peak in any of 2023-2025 (FINDING-miso89 sec.8). Closing this needs a primary OEM/NREL ambient-derate citation for the two magnitudes, not a new mechanism.

disclosures.note: See metrics.json determination + reasons. This is a CONSISTENCY re-derivation adopted on CORRECTNESS, not on the residual (rules 1 / 11 / 19 / 23), and it is measured NEAR-INERT on the annual load-weighted mean: 2023 +$0.0001, 2024 +$0.0025, 2025 -$0.0007 against the miso-93 re-audit arm. C3a-2024 therefore stays FAIL (-10.06% -> -10.05%), exactly as the charter pre-registered ('this arm does NOT close C3a-2024'). The charter's SIGN for 2024 was wrong and is recorded as such: it predicted a small DECREASE from the block's net -362 MW of derate, and the measured move is a small INCREASE, because the overlays compose MULTIPLICATIVELY per (plant_code, plant_group) -- removing a double-derate from a plant the short overlay already holds near zero buys back little, while the +735 MW of new ST_GAS/CC_CHP rows bite in full. The double-count was thus largely inert in EFFECT while still a real correctness violation. LEDGERED and inherited from miso-81/86/88/90: {C3a-2025, C3b-2025, C3c 2023/2024/2025} plus the two storage benchmark-basis limitations. thermal_tranches_MISO.csv also consumes the changed extract and is also stale, but was deliberately NOT re-derived here: it does not reproduce at HEAD on its own pre-guard input (committed_pct differs on 71 plants, max 53.3 pp; nameplate_mw on 6, max 1,028.6 MW), so adopting it would be a confounded arm. It is reported with its measurement as the next lane in charter section 4.

exceptions.metric: hours RT-expressible LMP > $200/MWh (C3c scarcity tail, actual RT hourly gate; Indiana Hub)
exceptions.magnitude: model 0h vs RT actual 30h (>$200, Indiana Hub); DA actual 1h
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (structural - MISO administrative ORDC/RCPF scarcity tail, not an emergent marginal-cost outcome even in MISO's own SCED; representation-frontier caveat, every admissible mechanism tried on record per rule #1)
exceptions.reason: MISO's real scarcity tail is an administrative stepped ORDC/RCPF curve DERIVED FROM a Monte-Carlo LOLP simulation over 10-30 min net-load/outage uncertainty (MISO Scarcity Pricing White Paper Mar-2024 §3.2.1; energy steps $1,100/$2,100 anchored to $3,500 VOLL, per-product reserve curves, BPM-002 Att.B §5.4; Potomac Economics IMM 2024 MISO SOM; OSTI 2424806). It prices probabilistic short-term risk a deterministic perfect-foresight hourly LP does not contain; the generic PCM literature confirms deterministic LPs systematically under-produce the spike tail (arXiv 2101.02303, 23/23-model survey; PyPSA-Eur arXiv 2606.16486). Empirical confirmation on the miso-81 keeper's OWN hourly output: in the 88 actual 2025 Indiana-Hub RT>$200 hours the model prices ~$50 median / $157 max, the reserve adder fires 2/88, energy+reserve>$200 in 1/88, zero load-shed; those hours are mostly low in the DA market (e.g. RT $1,598 / DA $99), and a deterministic LP ~= the DA market, so it cannot manufacture them. Reaching the tail would require MANUFACTURING the uncertainty (rules #1/#10 forbid the fitted path); layering an ORDC/RCPF adder would fire ~2 hours, not the actual count. Frontier designation 2026-07-20: every named admissible mechanism tried on record and adopted (reserve deliverability / 10-min ramp caps miso-39; Midwest sub-regional reserves miso-71; measured reserve requirements miso-56); further work needs a NEW admissible measured identification, its own charter. NEVER an offer adder tuned to the tail. See docs/multi-iso/miso-scarcity-tail-external-validation-2026-07.md + docs/multi-iso/miso-scarcity-tail-diagnosis.md.

exceptions.reason: The 2025 annual-mean miss is the arithmetic tail of the C3c residual, NOT an independent level error: 2023 (-2.2%) and 2024 (-8.0%) both PASS; only 2025 fails, and 2025 carries the largest actual RT>$200 count (88 hrs). Those 88 Indiana-Hub spike hours (actual up to $1,783; model ~$50 median) contribute the bulk of the $6.73/MWh gap between the actual load-weighted mean $45.39 and the model $38.66. Closes only DOWNSTREAM of C3c (never via an offer/level adder tuned to the mean) - the same administrative Monte-Carlo-LOLP ORDC/RCPF tail a deterministic perfect-foresight LP cannot form (rules #1/#10). Frontier designation 2026-07-20; see the C3c ledger entries above + docs/multi-iso/miso-scarcity-tail-external-validation-2026-07.md. miso-88 note: the widening is the expected cost of a structurally-correct input and is KEPT per rule 1 -- the accurate heat rate stays in even though it worsens this crossing. Per rule 11 the worse fit is a discovered-bug signal to root-cause separately (the 2025 summer-body price formation lane, FINDING-miso87-c3b-summer-2025-body-2026-07.md), never to be offset with a tuned adder.

exceptions.metric: C3b monthly load-weighted price NRMSE (RT load-weighted actual, bench avgLMP.rt_lw_mon; Indiana Hub basis)
exceptions.magnitude: NRMSE 0.208 vs <=0.20 target/commercial (coincident band). 2025 ONLY - 2023 (0.081) and 2024 (0.129) both PASS comfortably. Located and sized: a ~10 GW under-derate of 2025 summer-peak fossil availability, driving a $16.3/MWh Jun+Jul HE16-18 body-peak shortfall against a diurnal spread the model reproduces at only 29-47% in every season of every year.
exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (structural - instrument-blocked measurement gap: the only record of the missing ~10 GW of 2025 summer-peak unavailability is published at a grain, region x cause and fuel-blind, that two prior charters proved cannot be attributed onto units without inventing the attribution; representation-frontier caveat, every enumerated instrument refuted, adjudicated data-blocked, or measured inert per rule #1)
exceptions.reason: INSTRUMENT-BLOCKED MEASUREMENT GAP, adjudicated NO-BUILD by miso-89 and ledgered on owner decision 2026-07-26. Full evidence: results/calibration/FINDING-miso89-diurnal-spread-compression-2026-07.md (scored from committed artifacts and the model's own data path only - keeper hourly/ sidecars, the run payload's lmpDeltaHr, bench/MISO/, data/raw/_validation-source/actual_lmp_hourly_zonal_MISO.parquet; no LP re-solve). (1) IT IS NOT A 2025 LEVEL MISS - it is standing DIURNAL-SPREAD COMPRESSION. Peak (HE16-18) minus night (HE01-03), body-censored at $200, model/actual ratio: winter 0.39/0.29/0.30, shoulder 0.33/0.35/0.36, summer 0.45/0.47/0.37 (2023/2024/2025). The model reproduces 29-47% of the observed diurnal spread in EVERY season of EVERY year. 2025 breaches the veto only because the ACTUAL summer spread widened (26.3 -> 30.1 -> 32.7 $/MWh) while the model's stayed flat (11.7 -> 14.2 -> 12.2). Both ends miss in OPPOSITE directions (Jun+Jul, body <=$200): night model-actual +8.1/+5.6/+7.5, peak -5.9/-11.9/-16.3. In 2023 they nearly cancel in the monthly mean (June delta +0.4); by 2025 the peak-side error dominates because C3b is LOAD-WEIGHTED. The metric changed; the model's error did not. (2) THE MISS IS A ~10 GW 2025 SUMMER-PEAK FOSSIL UNDER-DERATE. Model fossil derate at Jun/Jul HE16-18 is flat across years - 20.07 / 19.07 / 20.83 GW (+1.76 GW into 2025) - while MISO's own published offline record jumps 35.10 / 33.27 / 45.59 GW (+12.32). The offset is stable at ~14.6 GW in 2023/2024 (the expected non-fossil share plus CT blindness) and BREAKS to 24.76 GW in 2025. This is a DIFFERENCE-IN-DIFFERENCES argument, so it does NOT require attributing the published total across fuels - the miso-87 cross-fuel refutation is respected; it requires only that the non-fossil share did not itself jump ~10 GW. And 2025 was NOT hot: MISO zone-mean daily TMAX at summer peak 29.6 / 29.2 / 29.8 C, with cheap gas ($3.33-3.52/MMBtu). Normal temperatures, cheap fuel - a SUPPLY-SIDE tightening of roughly 12 GW the model cannot see. (3) IT IS A BODY PHENOMENON, DISTINCT FROM THE C3c TAIL - it is NOT that ledger entry widened. Implied marginal heat rate at summer peak (body-censored at $200, price / the model's own MISO delivered gas): model 9.0 / 11.4 / 13.4 vs actual 10.4 / 15.3 / 18.1 MMBtu/MWh. At 18.1 the 2025 actual summer BODY peak sits far above the marginal cost of the worst physical unit in MISO's fleet (legacy CT 11.5, ST_GAS ~13): the real summer-peak body price is RENT, not fuel x heat rate. The model tops out at 13.4 because P1 start-up amortization is the only thing it carries above physical cost. (4) IT CANNOT BE CLOSED BY ADDING A PRICING MECHANISM - MISO's scarcity apparatus is ALREADY BUILT, ALREADY ON, AND STARVED, NOT MISSING. Live in this keeper: energy_reserve_coopt, miso_measured_reserve_requirements (market-wide mean 2.64 / max 3.30 GW, 2025), miso_zonal_reserves, miso_midwest_subregional_reserves, miso_reserve_pergen, and _miso_design's demand curve ramping to MISO_RESERVE_DEMAND_CURVE_MAX = $3,500/MWh. The reserve shadow price is non-zero in 0 / 6 / 2 hours out of 8760; the curve never leaves its flat segment. Layering a second price-formation mechanism on a phenomenon that already has one is forbidden by rule 17. (5) AND NO AVAILABILITY FIX OF PLAUSIBLE SIZE CAN ARM IT. At Jun/Jul HE16-18 2025 the model carries 97.46 GW of available fossil against 65.57 GW dispatched - 31.9 GW of idle headroom, 49% above dispatch - versus a 2.64 GW reserve requirement, and the solve's own log reports an availability-scaled 10-min deliverable ramp cap of mean 37,088 / min 32,322 MW. Reserve supply exceeds requirement by more than 12x. Even a generous 15% additional CT derate removes only ~3.4 GW of that 31.9 GW, leaves the reserve constraint slack by ~10x, still never prices the RDC, and at the measured local stack slope (~2 $/GW) is worth ~$4-6 of the $16.3 peak-hour gap. (6) THE MODEL'S SUPPLY STACK IS NEARLY FLAT, which is why the spread cannot widen: median model price by 2025-summer thermal-dispatch ventile runs $28.6 (33.8 GW) / $33.3 (48.1) / $36.2 (56.1) / $41.8 (65.3) / $52.4 (72.9) - $24 across a 39 GW range, ~0.6 $/GW average and 2.0 $/GW at the steepest ventile, with no convexity at the top. (7) CONGESTION IS NOT THE DRIVER AND CANNOT BE. C3b scores the LOAD-WEIGHTED ISO mean, and a load-weighted-zero deviation pattern cannot move a load-weighted mean. Verified as a diagnostic decomposition (not a proposed input): imposing the ACTUAL hourly zonal deviation-from-ISO-mean on the model's own level leaves NRMSE identical to three decimals - 0.081 / 0.129 / 0.206. The zonal-spread defect is real (model summer-peak zonal spread $1.6 vs actual $32.5) and is separately unledgered and worth its own entry, but it is NOT this failure; it is independently adjudicated NO-BUILD/data-blocked (miso-78 sec.3, RO-3 killed empirically by miso-79: intra-LBA mass 88-99.7%, even a ~12-zone model converts only ~1.9-3.8%). (8) INSTRUMENT ENUMERATION - ALL CLOSED. Published MISO total with uniform attribution: REJECTED (miso-85 - over-derates CTs, manufacturing a 138 h >$200 tail, and under-derates coal, C1 COAL_PRB +28.3 TWh). Cross-fuel attribution of that total: REFUTED at charter (miso-87, two independent grounds). Zone refinement / congestion representation: NO-BUILD, data-blocked (miso-78/79). temp_dependent_derate: REJECTED (refuted for the ERCOT gas fleet 2026-07-09). gt_ambient_derate: PROVABLY INERT for MISO - measured, zone-mean TMAX exceeds its 35 C reference in 24 h of 2023 and 0 h of 2024/2025, and 0 h at summer peak in ANY year, so it removes 0 MW in the failing window. CT-specific measured availability: NO SOURCE at CT grain - CTs are CEMS-blind by construction and MISO publishes region x cause only. unit_partial_outage_windows: PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD - the detector targets plants WITHOUT unit-level data, and MISO already carries 95.4% coal / 90.1% CC unit-level coverage. No enumerated instrument remains; continuing to probe would be searching for a mechanism to hit a number, which rules 1/10 forbid. (9) WHAT THIS ENTRY DOES NOT LICENSE. NOT an offer adder, summer multiplier, or residual-tuned band (rules 1/10). NOT widening the C3c price_tail ledger to absorb it - per (3) this is a body phenomenon and per (4) the tail apparatus is present, not absent; it carries its own evidence or none. NOT re-opening any (8) refutation without new external facts of the class those charters specify. NOT a fitted availability number - per rule 24 a tuned value is an answer key, not a parameter. (10) THE UNBLOCKING DATUM, and the standing data ask opened alongside this entry (owner decision 2026-07-26, option 2): MISO outage data at UNIT or FUEL grain - a GADS-derived class series, or the IMM's unit-level outage appendix if obtainable. Rule 22 permits training-year intake under session-logged owner authorization. Until such a source exists this lane cannot be built honestly. Charter: docs/handoffs/miso-outage-grain-data-ask-2026-07.md. (11) MAGNITUDE PROVENANCE. The 0.204 -> 0.208 widening between the miso-86 and miso-88 keepers was PRE-REGISTERED in the miso-88 charter sec.5 before solving, as the arithmetic consequence of returning 534.8 MW of correctly-priced CC to the merit order below coal. It is KEPT per rules 1/11 - the accurate eGRID boundary heat rate stays in even though it worsens this crossing, and the worse fit is treated as a discovered-bug signal root-caused here, never offset with a tuned adder.
